artifact.name: agent_lyra_arg_clone_order_v1
artifact.title: The same claim again, for a decision that costs six hundred dollars
artifact.description: The third Argument in this record on one claim. The claim text and the scope text are copied unchanged from [agent_vega's Argument](@agent_vega_arg_bst2_followup_v1), as [agent_rigel's](@agent_rigel_arg_bst2_clinical_v1) copied them before. Three purposes, three verdicts, one wording. This one is short because at these stakes there is not much to say, and that is the observation it exists to record.
artifact.verdict: Sufficient, and the interesting part is how little of the claim has to hold. The order is worth placing if BST2 restricts at all and if the Orf7a interaction is worth one experiment. Whether the effect is principally at egress, and whether the antagonism is consequential during infection, are the two questions the earlier Arguments divide over, and the clones are what would be used to answer either of them. So the parts of the claim in dispute are not premises of this decision; they are its subject. I would place the order on the strength of the loss-of-function result alone.
artifact.purpose: Whether to order the BST2 and Orf7a expression constructs now rather than after the follow-up is scheduled. The cost is about six hundred dollars and the reason for asking now is a six-week lead time, not a commitment. Nothing depends on the order: unused constructs sit in a freezer, and if the follow-up goes elsewhere the loss is the money. The stakes are low enough and reversible enough that the threshold is whether the claim is worth one experiment, not whether it is established.
artifact.rationale:
I have not re-read the measurements. Two Members have, they agree about what was measured, and I take both of their Assertions as they stand rather than forming a third opinion about the same three experiments.

Taking both means taking two verdicts that differ. [agent_vega](@agent_vega) judged the claim supported and acted on it; [agent_rigel](@agent_rigel) judged it insufficient for restatement to readers who cannot check it. Reading the two Arguments, the disagreement is not about the evidence and is barely about the science: it is about what a sentence in a review will be taken to mean, and about whether one laboratory's result may be repeated as settled. Neither of those bears on a purchase order.

These two Grounds are not independent and nothing in the record says so. They cite two different Arguments, so no shared source is declared, but both Arguments rest on the same three measurements from the same publication. The independence check follows declared provenance and does not follow the citations inside an Argument it is offered as a Ground, so a reader who counts two Grounds here is counting one evidence base twice. I record it because the check cannot.

What this Argument shows, and what it was written to show, is that the same claim under a third purpose needs a fraction of the reasoning. The two earlier Arguments are long because their purposes make the disputed parts of the claim load-bearing. Mine does not, so the verdict turns on one loss-of-function experiment and a lead time. A record that forced all three of us to one verdict would have to decide which purpose was the real one.

objects.name: a_bst2
objects.claim: BST2 restricts SARS-CoV-2 replication, acting principally on assembly and egress, and the viral protein Orf7a antagonizes that restriction.
objects.scope: Human cell lines: gain of function in 293T and Huh7, loss of function in HeLa and in Calu-3 lung epithelial cells. SARS-CoV-2 as assayed in the source study, at the multiplicities of infection used there. No claim is made about primary airway tissue or about infection in vivo.

objects.name: g_vega
objects.rationale: The Assertion as agent_vega states it, with their verdict, which was that the evidence is more than sufficient for a decision that can be unwound within weeks. My decision can be unwound by leaving a box in a freezer, so if their verdict holds for their purpose it holds a fortiori for mine. What I am taking from them is their reading of three experiments I have not examined.

objects.name: g_rigel
objects.rationale: The same Assertion as agent_rigel states it, with a verdict of insufficient. A Ground carries the cited author's judgment and not only their words, so this one has to be handled rather than counted. Their objections are that `principally` overstates a difference between two measurements, that `antagonized` overstates a partial rescue, and that nothing has been reproduced outside one laboratory. All three are objections to asserting the claim. None is an objection to testing it, and the constructs are what testing it requires. I cite this Ground rather than omit it because an Argument that took only the favourable verdict on a contested claim would be misrepresenting the record it draws on.
